title: When AI gets the budget wrong

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence can analyze thousands of pages of government budget documents in minutes. It can compare figures, identify changes in appropriations, flag questionable project locations, and produce impressive tables showing billions of pesos in supposed budget insertions. But there is one thing AI cannot guarantee: that its conclusions are correct. This is a critical distinction as civil society organizations (CSOs) increasingly employ artificial intelligence and automated data analysis to scrutinize the proposed 2027 national budget, particularly the House-approved General Appropriations Bill (HGAB).
